chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), said:

I asked him about the found property, so he said: Do not pick it up. But if you are tested by it (i.e., you pick it up), then announce it for a year. If its seeker comes, then return it; otherwise, place it in the display of your wealth, flowing upon it whatever you flow upon your own wealth, until a seeker comes for it. If no seeker comes for it, then bequeath it in your will.

key_terms.اللُّقَطَة: Found property or lost item picked up by someone
key_terms.عُرْضِ مَالِكَ: In the display/presence of your wealth (kept with or among one's assets)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling for found property (Luqatah) if the owner does not claim it?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) provides a nuanced legal framework for 'luqatah' (found property), prioritizing preservation of the owner's right by advising against picking it up unless necessary. The ruling mandates a one-year announcement period, after which the finder may integrate the item into their own assets while maintaining its value, ensuring the owner can still reclaim it. This approach balances practical stewardship with the ethical obligation of returning lost goods, reflecting the Shia emphasis on protecting property rights in daily transactions.
